 ## Chapter 2 Stances (Ma) and Footwork (Jeun Ma)
Wing Chun’s combat effectiveness is dependent on three stance and footwork features. 

- ***Mobility***  is the practitioner’s ability to move quickly and safely from one stance to another in defense and the ability to bridge the gap safely in attack. 

- ***Stability*** is the practitioner’s ability to maintain balance while generating power in strikes through grounded strong stances and maintaining their own balance while destroying their opponent’s balance. 

- ***Interruptibility*** is the practitioner’s ability to interrupt movements and techniques at any point.

### <a id="sf_stances"></a>Stances (Ma)
#### Yee Jee Keem Yeung Ma (Goat Squeezing Stance)
![][gss]

### Neutral Stance
The neutral stance is non-commitment to movement. The weight is balanced between both legs permitting easy movement in any direction. The neutral stance is characterized by the feet being approximately shoulder width apart. The weight is evenly distributed between both legs. The knees are flexed which makes you squat slightly, lowering your center of gravity and improving your stability.
|Neutral|
|:---:|
|![][ns]|
### Neutral Side Stance
In the neutral side stance the feet are a normal stepping distance apart and weight is distributed evenly on both legs. The designation as to left or right neutral side stance is dependant on which foot is pointing forward. In the right neutral side stance the right foot is pointing forward and the left leg is turned at the hip so that the foot and knee are pointing at approximately 68° away from forward. For the left neutral side stance the feet positions are reversed.

### Exchange Stance

Used as a very brief transitory stance between side changes.

### <a id="sf_footwork"></a> Footwork (Jeun Ma)
The feet are never slid or dragged along the ground. They are always raised and lowered with control. When changing stances the practitioner switches his stance from one side to the other smoothly and quickly. When moving forward the knee is raised and brought through the centerline to protect the groin and shield against low attacks.
